ABC.h: A · THE CHANGE, UP TO NOW
items: has **got / gotten** -er
has **become** more …
… **than it used to be**
**not as** … **as**
is **getting** -er and -er
**more and more** …
one syllable, or two syllables ending in -y: green → **greener**, busy → **busier**, pricey → **pricier**
most other words: **more** crowded, **more** modern
quieter / more quiet · livelier / more lively
good → **better** · bad → **worse**
-er OR more, never both: busier — not ~~more busier~~
going down: **less** + the plain form: less green, less safe

blocks.instr: Ask each other. Start your answer with a phrase from the box, then say the rest any way you can.
items: **1**  **Has the place where you grew up changed much?** ((In what way? What’s one thing that’s different now? Haven’t been back in a while? Say what you’ve heard.))
**2**  **And the place where you live now — has it changed since you moved there?** ((Never moved? Talk about a place you go to a lot.))
blocks.fast: Think of a place you know that has hardly changed. What’s still the same there?

blocks.instr: Take turns: think of a place you know well and say how it’s changed. Use one word from each card: It’s got / gotten a lot … Then tap the card to check.

cards.front: **green**  ↔  **built-up** ((more trees and parks · houses where there used to be fields))
cards.back: It’s got / gotten a lot **greener**. · It’s got / gotten a lot **more built-up**.

cards.front: **busy**  ↔  **quiet** ((more people, more traffic · not as many cars))
cards.back: It’s got / gotten a lot **busier**. · It’s got / gotten a lot **quieter** / **more quiet**.

cards.front: **crowded**  ↔  **empty** ((you can’t move on Saturdays · hardly anyone on the streets after six))
cards.back: It’s got / gotten a lot **more crowded**. · It’s got / gotten a lot **emptier**.

cards.front: **clean**  ↔  **dirty** ((clean streets now · trash on the streets))
cards.back: It’s got / gotten a lot **cleaner**. · It’s got / gotten a lot **dirtier**.

cards.front: **safe**  ↔  **dangerous** ((you can walk home at night · you don’t go out alone at night))
cards.back: It’s got / gotten a lot **safer**. · It’s got / gotten a lot **more dangerous**.

cards.front: **fancy**  ↔  **run-down** ((cocktail bars instead of cheap cafés · peeling paint, broken windows))
cards.back: It’s got / gotten a lot **fancier**. · It’s got / gotten a lot **more run-down**.

cards.front: **pricey**  ↔  **affordable** ((eight euros for a coffee! · rents have gone down))
cards.back: It’s got / gotten a lot **pricier**. · It’s got / gotten a lot **more affordable**.
It’s got / gotten a lot **livelier** / **more lively**.
It’s got / gotten a lot **more touristy**.
It’s got / gotten a lot **more modern**.

cards.front: **good**  ↔  **bad** ((a new park, a new metro line · more crime, more traffic jams))
cards.back: It’s got / gotten a lot **better**. · It’s got / gotten a lot **worse**.

blocks.instr: Take turns: make a sentence from the words — the grey line is a clue. Say it aloud, then tap the card to check. Then both of you talk about yourselves.
blocks.instr_next: And this one? Then talk about yourselves.

cards.front: **the station · nice** ((they renovated it last year))
cards.back: The station **has got / gotten a lot nicer**. ((also fine: has become a lot nicer))
cards.turn: A place near you that has got / gotten a lot nicer — or a lot worse. What happened?

cards.front: **TVs · cheap** ((you pay much less now than twenty years ago))
cards.back: TVs **are a lot cheaper than they used to be**. ((also fine: TVs have got / gotten a lot cheaper.))
cards.turn: Two things that are a lot cheaper — or a lot more expensive — than they used to be. Which one do you notice most?

cards.back: The summers **are getting hotter and hotter**.
cards.turn: Two things that are getting better and better — or worse and worse — where you live. Which one matters most to you?

cards.front: **my favourite restaurant · good** ((it was better ten years ago))
cards.back: My favourite restaurant **isn’t as good as it used to be**. ((also fine: … isn’t as good as it was.))
cards.turn: A café, a shop or a TV show that isn’t as good as it used to be. What’s changed?

cards.front: **the old town · touristy** ((souvenir shops everywhere now))
cards.back: The old town **has become a lot more touristy**. ((also fine: … is a lot more touristy than it used to be.))
cards.turn: A place that has become a lot more touristy — or one that hasn’t changed at all. Why do you think that is?

cards.front: **my street · noisy** ((a new bar opens every month))
cards.back: My street **is getting noisier and noisier**.
cards.turn: What’s getting more and more popular where you live? Who’s happy about it, and who isn’t?

scenes.example: **Yes and no.** It’s **pretty much the same** street — even the tree is still there — but it’s **got** / **gotten** a lot **nicer**.
Yes, it has, actually. It’s **got** / **gotten** a lot **nicer** since they closed it to cars — and **a lot livelier**.

scenes.example: Yes and no. The street is **pretty much the same**, but it’s **a lot greener**, and the old building on the corner is gone.
**Not really, no.** From up on the hill, it’s **pretty much the same**.

blocks.instr: At the start of the lesson, you answered this question in the chat. How would you answer it now? Take turns. Try not to look at the box.
task: **1**  Your partner asks: **Has the place where you grew up changed much?** ((Haven’t been back in a while? Say what you’ve heard — or talk about where you live now.))
**2**  Answer, then give details: how it’s changed, how it compares with the past, and what’s still changing.
**Is that a good thing?** Why (not)? ((— if you don’t say how you feel about it))
**Where do you hear about it — family, friends, social media?** ((— if you don’t live there now))
